processed.definition: Learning from interaction（从交互中学习）是一种通过智能体与环境的直接交互来获取关于因果、行为后果与目标达成等知识的学习方式，被视为几乎所有学习与智能理论的基础理念，也是强化学习等计算框架从经验中构建学习算法的核心出发点。

supporting_observations.support: 源文明确指出 'we learn by interacting with our environment'，并列举婴儿玩耍、学开车、学对话等例子说明交互产生关于因果、行为后果和目标的知识；原文还以原话 'Learning from interaction is a foundational idea underlying nearly all theories of learning and intelligence' 直接支撑'几乎所有学习与智能理论的基础理念'这一表述，同时该书以此为起点探索计算学习方法，支撑'强化学习等计算框架的出发点'这一补充。

processed.definition: 计算方法（computational approach）是一种以人工智能研究者或工程师视角研究学习问题的方法论，不直接理论化人或动物的实际学习机制，而是在理想化的学习情境中通过数学分析或计算实验评估各种学习方法的有效性。它侧重于为科学或经济上感兴趣的学习问题设计有效的机器解决方案，强化学习即是该方法论框架下的一种具体研究路径。

supporting_observations.support: 原文将计算方法明确界定为本书研究学习问题所采用的方法论（'we explore a computational approach to learning from interaction'），并以AI研究者/工程师视角、不直接理论化生物学习、以数学分析或计算实验评估方法有效性作为其核心特征；末尾进一步说明该方法论下本书所探索的具体路径被称为强化学习。

processed.definition: 强化学习是一类面向目标的机器学习范式，让智能体在与环境的持续交互中通过试错和评价性奖赏信号学习将状态映射到动作以最大化累积回报；与监督学习依赖带正确答案的指导性反馈不同，它依赖对所采取动作的纯评价性反馈，因而需要主动探索。

supporting_observations.support: 锚定原始定义核心：'goal-directed learning from interaction'比其他机器学习方法更受强调，确认'面向目标、从交互中学习'是身份边界要素，并明确与其他 ML 方法的对比关系。
提供最权威的核心定义（mapping situations to actions to maximize a numerical reward signal），并明确试错搜索与延迟回报是强化学习两个最重要的区别性特征；同时指出 RL 同时是问题、一类求解方法与研究领域这一三重身份。
给出面向目标的学习与决策的计算方法定义，并强调其'通过与环境直接交互学习、不需要示范性监督、不需要完整环境模型'的区分性特征，与监督学习/规划形成对比。
明确强化学习与其他学习类型最重要的区别——使用评价所采取动作的训练信息而非给出正确动作的指导性信息，由此产生对主动探索的需要，支撑定义中与监督学习的对比与'试错/评价性反馈'要素。
通过示例总结 RL 的共性特征：主动决策智能体与环境的交互、在环境不确定条件下追求目标、动作影响未来状态、需要考虑延迟后果；为定义中'智能体—环境—目标—评价性反馈'框架提供事实依据。

processed.definition: 目标导向学习是一种以达成目标为导向、通过与环境交互来获取经验的学习范式，通常被用来描述强化学习相较于其他机器学习方法更为侧重的学习取向，而非等同于强化学习本身。

supporting_observations.support: 原文模型引文 'The approach we explore, called reinforcement learning, is much more focused on goal-directed learning from interaction than are other approaches to machine learning' 直接给出了该概念的核心含义（goal-directed learning from interaction）以及它与强化学习的关系（强化学习对其更为侧重），并将其标注为'学习范式'类别，为当前定义提供唯一直接支持。

processed.definition: 试错搜索（trial-and-error search / learning）是一种学习范式：学习者不预先获得正确动作的指导，而是通过尝试各种动作并依据环境返回的评价性反馈来发现能带来最大回报的行为。它是强化学习的两大区分性特征之一（与延迟回报并列），在实现上对应于无模型方法（与基于模型的规划相对），并与有"正确答案"标签的监督学习形成对照。

supporting_observations.support: 原文将 trial-and-error search 与 delayed reward 并列为强化学习的两大区分性特征，并给出"学习者不被告知应采取哪个动作，而必须通过尝试来发现能带来最大回报的动作"的标准定义，为义项提供核心表述与"区分性特征"定位。
原文给出试错学习的"本质特征"——"依据评价性反馈来选择动作，而不依赖关于正确动作的知识"，并与监督学习形成对照，锚定义项中"评价性反馈"与"不预先获得正确动作"两个关键含义。
原文将 trial-and-error learning 定位为无模型方法的特征（"viewed as almost the opposite of planning"），并指出现代强化学习从低层试错学习到高层规划是一个连续谱，支持义项中"无模型方法"与"基于模型的规划"对照。
原文通过 Thorndike 效果律刻画试错学习为"尝试多种替代方案并通过比较其后果进行选择"的选择性过程，并指出强化学习算法的选择性与此对应，为义项提供"选择/评价"机制与心理学根源的支持。
原文追溯试错学习思想可至 19 世纪动物学习心理学（Alexander Bain、Conway Lloyd Morgan），为义项提供历史与跨学科背景。

processed.definition: 延迟奖励是强化学习区别于其他学习范式的核心特征之一，指智能体当前采取的动作不仅影响即时奖励，还会改变下一时刻所处的状态，并由此影响该状态之后所有后续奖励，因而在求解时必须权衡即时奖励与延迟奖励。

supporting_observations.support: 原文将延迟奖励与试错搜索并列为强化学习最重要的两个区分特征，并直接给出核心定义：动作可能不仅影响即时奖励，还影响下一状态并经此影响所有后续奖励，为本义项的核心内涵提供直接锚定。
该段在有限马尔可夫决策过程的形式化语境中进一步指出 MDP 涉及 delayed reward，并强调需要 trade off 即时与延迟奖励，为定义中“权衡即时与延迟奖励”这一补充特征提供原文依据。

processed.definition: 奖励信号是强化学习中由环境在每个时间步发送给智能体的标量数值（通常记为 Rt，可为正、负或零），用于形式化定义学习问题的目标，智能体的唯一长期目标就是最大化所收到的奖励信号在长期内的累计值；它与驱动学习算法参数更新的"强化信号"（如 TD 误差）相区分——强化信号常由奖励信号与其他项（如价值差）共同构成，而奖励信号本身只是定义问题而非直接驱动学习。

supporting_observations.support: 原文将强化学习定义为通过试错以'最大化一个数值奖励信号'来学习将情境映射到动作的方式，锚定了奖励信号作为'被最大化目标的数值信号'这一核心义项。
明确指出'每个时间步环境向智能体发送一个称为奖励的单一数值'，'奖励信号定义了强化学习问题的目标'，并强调它是'改变策略的主要依据'，支持定义中'由环境发送的标量、定义目标'的描述。
给出形式化表述：奖励是'从环境传递到智能体的特殊信号'，'每个时间步奖励是一个简单数值 Rt ∈ R'，智能体目标是'在长期最大化奖励总量'，并把它与作为强化学习最显著特征之一联系起来，支撑定义中 Rt 记号与'长期累计最大化'的描述。
明确区分'奖励信号'与'强化信号'，并指出对部分算法强化信号就等于奖励信号，但多数算法中强化信号还包含如 TD 误差等额外项，支撑定义中'奖励信号与强化信号相区分'的比较说明。
将强化学习的奖励信号刻画为'标量 Rt'，并把它与大脑中'主奖励信号'的假说对比，支撑定义中标量性与 Rt 记号的表述。

processed.definition: 监督学习是机器学习的基本范式之一，通过外部监督者提供的带标签训练样本（每个样本包含一个情境描述及其对应的正确动作或类别标签）进行学习，目标是使系统能够泛化到训练集未覆盖的新情境给出正确响应；其训练信号是指示性的（直接告知正确动作），与依赖评估性反馈的强化学习以及在无标签数据中发现隐藏结构的无监督学习形成对比。

supporting_observations.support: 提供候选实体的原始规范定义，明确指出监督学习从外部监督者提供的带标签训练样本学习，目标是泛化到训练集之外的情境，并在此处与强化学习和无监督学习作为三大机器学习范式进行对比。
明确指出监督学习的反馈是'纯指导性的'（独立于实际采取的动作，直接指示正确动作），与强化学习的评估性反馈形成对比；并列举其涵盖范围包括模式分类、人工神经网络和系统辨识。
从操作角度补充监督学习的实现方式——学习模仿输入—输出样本（当输出为数值时也称函数逼近），与 definition 中'带标签训练样本'和'泛化'的核心概念一致。
进一步刻画监督学习的本质：'联想性的但非选择性的，因为它依赖直接告诉智能体如何改变行为的指令'，与 definition 中'指示性反馈'和'外部监督者提供标签'一致。

processed.definition: 无监督学习是机器学习中的一种范式，通常旨在从无标签数据集合中发现隐藏的结构。它与监督学习（依赖标注样本）和强化学习（以最大化奖励信号为目标）相区别，核心任务是从未标注数据中挖掘内在模式而非预测标签或优化回报。

supporting_observations.support: 原文 model_quote 直接给出无监督学习的通常定义（finding structure hidden in collections of unlabeled data），并通过与强化学习的对比明确其目标是发现隐藏结构而非最大化奖励信号，同时确认它是与监督学习、强化学习并立的独立机器学习范式。

processed.definition: 马尔可夫决策过程（Markov Decision Process，MDP）是一种在不确定性下进行序贯决策的数学形式化框架，通过具有马尔可夫性的状态、动作、奖励与转移概率刻画智能体与环境的离散时间步交互。它在强化学习中作为最优控制和目标导向学习的基础模型，由 Bellman 于 1957 年从离散随机最优控制问题中引入。

supporting_observations.support: 提供了教材对 MDP 的奠基性定义：形式化框架，涵盖感知、动作、目标三个最简方面，用于把强化学习形式化为对不完全已知的 MDP 的最优控制。
明确 MDP 通过状态、动作和奖励定义智能体与环境的交互，并体现因果、不确定性与非确定性、显式目标等基本特征。
锚定历史起源与上位类别：Bellman 1957 年将其作为离散随机最优控制问题引入。
给出典型的智能体-环境离散时间步交互形式：每步智能体依据状态选择动作，环境返回新状态与数值奖励。
给出概念的操作性界定：当强化学习设定具备良好定义的转移概率时即构成 MDP，从而把马尔可夫性与转移概率写为概念的核心要素。

processed.definition: Optimal control is a branch of control theory concerned with designing a controller to minimize or maximize a measure of a dynamical system's behavior over time; it is the field from which Markov decision processes and dynamic programming originated and that provides the formal framework underlying reinforcement learning.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the canonical definition ('designing a controller to minimize or maximize a measure of a dynamical system's behavior over time'), the historical dating (term came into use in the late 1950s), and the link to Bellman, dynamic programming, and MDPs.
Identifies optimal control as the field from which MDPs originated and to which the RL problem is deeply indebted, establishing it as the formal parent discipline of RL.

Describes optimal control as a field of control theory developed in the 1950s by extending 19th-century state-function theories, reinforcing its identity as a mature control-theoretic discipline rather than an RL-specific concept.
Anchors the role of optimal control as the control-theoretic context in which RL is formalized, specifically as the optimal control of incompletely-known MDPs.
Index entry treating optimal control as the problem of finding a control law that optimizes a long-term objective and as a historical antecedent of reinforcement learning.

processed.definition: The fundamental trade-off in reinforcement learning between exploiting actions already known to produce high reward and exploring untried actions in order to improve future action selections, where a single action cannot be both exploratory and exploitative and neither can be pursued exclusively without failing the task. It is widely treated as a distinctive challenge of reinforcement learning (and related decision-making problems such as k-armed bandits) and also appears under names such as the exploration–exploitation trade-off, the dual control problem, or the identification-versus-control conflict in control engineering.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the core definition: the trade-off between exploiting tried-and-effective actions and exploring new ones, with the key claim that neither can be pursued exclusively without failing the task; also explicitly states it is a challenge unique to RL and 'remains unresolved'.

Sharpens the trade-off by showing that exploitation maximizes expected one-step reward while exploration may yield greater total reward in the long run, and introduces the 'conflict' framing because 'it is not possible both to explore and to exploit with any single action selection.'

Confirms the trade-off extends across the full range of bandit/RL algorithms (ε-greedy, UCB, gradient bandit, optimistic initialization) and that 'a fully satisfactory solution to the problem of balancing exploration and exploitation' is not yet available, reinforcing the 'distinctive challenge' claim.

Anchors cross-disciplinary equivalence by stating the same conflict is 'known in control engineering as the conflict between identification (or estimation) and control' and that Holland (1975) framed it for genetic algorithms as 'the conflict between the need to exploit and the need for new information.'

Demonstrates the trade-off is not limited to action selection but reappears in planning, where 'exploration means trying actions that improve the model, whereas exploitation means behaving in the optimal way given the current model,' supporting its identity as a general decision-making dilemma rather than a bandit-specific one.

processed.definition: Exploration is a core strategy in reinforcement learning in which an agent tries actions it has not selected before—or ones other than the currently estimated-best—so as to gather information about their values and discover potentially better actions. It is the natural counterpart to exploitation: exploration may reduce short-term reward, but is necessary for the agent to identify optimal actions under estimation uncertainty, stochastic rewards, or nonstationary conditions.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the foundational general definition: trying previously unselected actions to discover rewarding ones and enable better future action selections, introducing the exploration–exploitation trade-off in Chapter 1.
Operationalizes exploration in the k-armed bandit setting as selecting nongreedy actions to improve value estimates, and makes the long-term-versus-short-term reward trade-off explicit.

States the core motivation for exploration—uncertainty in action-value estimates—and motivates principled methods such as UCB action selection, showing the concept extends beyond ε-greedy to more directed exploration.

Shows exploration realized via optimistic initial values and explicitly notes a key limitation: some exploration mechanisms (e.g., optimism-driven) are inherently temporary and unsuitable for nonstationary tasks, confirming exploration as a broad class of behaviors.

Places exploration within the broader RL framework of search-and-memory and compares it to animal exploration, reinforcing that exploration is the action-selection component any RL algorithm requires and that its forms (ε-greedy, UCB, etc.) are merely instances of a general strategy.

processed.definition: In reinforcement learning, exploitation is the strategy of selecting the action currently estimated to be best based on the agent's accumulated knowledge, in order to obtain immediate reward. It is one side of the exploration–exploitation trade-off, favoring actions already known to yield high reward at the possible cost of discovering better long-term alternatives.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the general meaning of exploitation as preferring actions tried in the past and found effective at producing reward, and introduces the exploration–exploitation trade-off as a defining tension of the concept.

Anchors the formal greedy-action framing ('selecting a greedy action to use one's current knowledge of the action values') and the key trade-off that exploitation maximizes the expected one-step reward but may forgo greater total reward in the long run.

Reinforces that exploitation means selecting the action believed to have the highest value based on current estimates and explicitly frames it as one side of the balance that reinforcement learning must maintain against exploration.

processed.definition: In reinforcement learning, planning is any computational process that uses a model of the environment to produce or improve a policy or value function by considering or simulating possible future situations before they are actually experienced. It is the defining component of model-based methods, typically intermixed with real-time action selection, and is contrasted with model-free trial-and-error learning.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the canonical textbook definition: planning is 'any computational process that takes a model as input and produces or improves a policy for interacting with the modeled environment,' which directly anchors the core of the synthesized definition.

Defines planning as 'any way of deciding on a course of action by considering possible future situations before they are actually experienced' and explicitly frames model-based/planning methods as 'almost the opposite' of model-free trial-and-error learning, supporting the contrast and the 'simulating future situations' aspect.

Anchors the RL-specific framing that planning must address the interplay between planning and real-time action selection, as well as how environment models are acquired and improved — a constraint unique to the RL setting.

States that 'model-based methods rely on planning as their primary component, while model-free methods primarily rely on learning,' directly supporting the identification of planning as the defining component of model-based RL.

Distinguishes background planning from decision-time planning, capturing the two principal usage modes of planning within RL and reinforcing that planning is a process applied to a model to improve a policy or value function.

processed.definition: 目标导向智能体是强化学习中一个完整的、可与环境交互的目标寻求主体，具有明确目标，能感知环境的某些方面并选择动作来影响环境，且必须在环境存在显著不确定性的条件下运行。它不必是一个完整的有机体或机器人，也可以是更大行为系统中的一个组件，直接与该系统的其余部分交互、间接与该系统的环境交互。

supporting_observations.support: 原始定义直接出处的章节，明确给出'完整的、可交互的、目标寻求的智能体'的全部核心特征（明确目标、感知环境、选择动作、显著不确定性下运行），以及它不必是完整有机体/机器人、可以是更大行为系统组件的限定，全部直接支持当前 definition 的两个分句。
将强化学习定位为'由一个智能体通过与环境的直接交互来学习'的范式，并明确目标导向是该领域区别于其他计算方法的特征，支持将本概念锚定在强化学习框架中并强化其'目标导向'属性。
明确 RL 智能体的目标被形式化为最大化长期累积奖励（reward hypothesis），为 definition 中'具有明确目标'提供了具体的 RL 形式化支撑（目标=最大化累积奖励）。
给出'智能体—环境边界'的判定规则以及复杂机器人中可同时存在多个智能体的例子，直接支持 definition 中关于智能体/环境交互方式以及'可以是更大系统组件'的限定。

在全书后段再次重述'a reinforcement learning agent is not necessarily like a complete organism or robot; it can be a component of a larger behaving system'，与 observation 17 的限定相互印证，巩固 definition 第二句关于'不必是完整有机体/机器人'的边界。

processed.definition: In reinforcement learning, the environment is the external system outside the agent with which the agent continually interacts—sensing its state, taking actions that affect that state, and receiving numerical reward signals from it at each time step. The agent–environment boundary is defined by what the agent cannot change arbitrarily, so the environment is incompletely controllable and may or may not be completely known; it can also consist of the rest of a larger system together with that system's own external environment.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the foundational definition: the external system an agent interacts with over time, senses, and acts upon, and explicitly notes that an agent's environment can be the rest of a larger system together with its external environment.

Anchors the reward-delivery role: the environment sends the agent a single reward number each time step, and reward may be a stochastic function of state and actions—supporting the reward-signal clause in the definition.

Provides the canonical MDP formulation: 'The thing it interacts with, comprising everything outside the agent, is called the environment,' and confirms that it responds to actions with new states and rewards—supporting the 'everything outside the agent' framing.

Defines the agent–environment boundary by the criterion 'anything that cannot be changed arbitrarily by the agent is part of its environment' and treats reward computation as external—directly supporting the boundary definition and the incomplete-controllability claim.
States 'Its environment … is incompletely controllable and may or may not be completely known,' directly supporting the incomplete-controllability and knowledge clauses in the definition.

processed.definition: Curse of dimensionality is a term coined by Richard Bellman to describe the phenomenon whereby the computational or storage requirements of a problem grow exponentially with the number of dimensions or state variables. It manifests across multiple resources—including computation time in dynamic programming, the number of possible states, and memory for global approximations—and is commonly encountered in operations research, control theory, and machine learning, where scalable methods such as function approximation are used to mitigate it.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the Bellman attribution and the core characterization: computational requirements of dynamic programming grow exponentially with the number of state variables.
Anchors the state-space manifestation: the number of states grows exponentially with the number of state variables, and clarifies it is an inherent difficulty of the problem itself.
Anchors the memory/storage manifestation: a tabular global approximation in a k-dimensional state space requires memory exponential in k.
Locates the concept within operations research and control theory and supports the claim that scalable learning methods (e.g., parameterized approximators) are used to address it.

processed.definition: A parameterized function with a finite-dimensional weight vector, used in reinforcement learning to compactly approximate value functions, policies, or models when the number of states is too large to maintain a separate entry for each. It typically has far fewer parameters than states, so it can only represent a low-dimensional subspace of possible functions, and its weights are adjusted (for example by gradient-based methods) to better match observed targets.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the core identity as parameterized approximators used by reinforcement learning methods and motivates them by addressing the classical 'curse of dimensionality'.

Directly supports two key identifying features: having 'fewer parameters than states' and the practice of adjusting the parameters 'to better match the observed returns'; also names the targets as v_π and q_π.
Supports the 'compact' characterization and the broad scope of targets — value functions, policies, and models — when the state count far exceeds what a table can hold.

Supports the 'finite-dimensional weight vector' aspect (the policy is 'parameterized by a weight vector w') and situates the concept within Part II of the book, where function approximation is treated in detail.
Directly supports the 'far fewer parameters than states' feature and the consequence that the approximator defines 'a low-dimensional representable subspace of value functions'.

processed.definition: 弱方法（weak methods）是人工智能研究中对一类方法的统称，指基于搜索、学习等通用原理构建的方法，与依赖大量特定领域知识的“强方法”（strong methods）形成对比。

supporting_observations.support: P000016 中给出定义式表述——'基于通用原理（如搜索或学习）的方法被称为弱方法，而基于特定知识的方法被称为强方法'，并指出该区分源自20世纪60年代末AI研究的特定历史背景，直接锚定了弱方法作为AI方法分类概念的义项。

processed.definition: 强方法（strong methods）是人工智能中基于特定领域具体知识来求解问题的一类方法，与仅依赖搜索或学习等通用原理的弱方法（weak methods）相对。该术语源于20世纪60年代末AI研究中的一种观点，认为智能行为需要大量专门的技巧、过程和启发式知识作为支撑。

supporting_observations.support: 原文将强方法明确定义为'基于特定知识的方法'（those based on specific knowledge），并与弱方法（基于搜索或学习等通用原理）形成对比；同时指出该术语产生于60年代末的AI研究语境，且与'大量专门技巧、过程和启发式'的观点直接关联。

processed.definition: Operations research is an interdisciplinary field that uses mathematical modeling, statistical analysis, and optimization methods to support complex decision-making. It is a discipline in which the classical 'curse of dimensionality' is a well-known challenge, and it shares substantive methodological overlap with control theory, making it a natural point of interaction with reinforcement learning.

supporting_observations.support: Identifies operations research as a discipline in which the classical 'curse of dimensionality' arises and notes its connection to control theory and to reinforcement learning; this anchors the 'curse of dimensionality' and the RL-interaction claims in the definition.

processed.definition: Control theory is an interdisciplinary branch of engineering and mathematics that studies the modeling, analysis, and regulation of dynamical systems through feedback and control inputs. It is one of the classical settings in which the curse of dimensionality arises and it shares substantive and fruitful methodological interactions with reinforcement learning, which offers approximate methods for tackling problems of that scale.

supporting_observations.support: 源文本直接将 control theory 列为与强化学习存在"substantive and fruitful interactions"的工程与科学学科之一，并明确指出它和运筹学一样是经典"curse of dimensionality"出现的领域，这两事实锚定了定义中关于学科身份、与强化学习的互动以及维度灾难的论断。

processed.definition: Biological learning systems are the natural learning processes that occur in living organisms such as humans and other animals. They have been studied in neuroscience and psychology and have served as a foundational source of inspiration for many of the core algorithms of reinforcement learning.

supporting_observations.support: The source text directly states that 'many of the core algorithms of reinforcement learning were originally inspired by biological learning systems,' and situates these systems within biological organisms (humans and other animals), anchoring both the general meaning and the inspiration relationship with reinforcement learning.

processed.definition: 心理学是研究行为与心智过程的科学学科，传统上大量依赖实验室中的动物学习实验，后逐渐转向思维、推理等认知层面。在强化学习领域，心理学与之有长期且成果丰富的双向交叉：动物学习理论（如经典条件作用、操作性条件作用、Rescorla–Wagner 模型等）为强化学习算法提供了重要启发，而强化学习也反哺了更贴合经验数据的动物学习心理模型及脑奖励系统模型。

supporting_observations.support: 明确说明强化学习与心理学（含神经科学）有强烈且双向受益的交互，并指出强化学习贡献了更匹配经验数据的动物学习心理模型，锚定定义中关于 RL–心理学双向交叉的描述。
说明本书第三部分（含第 14 章）专门从动物学习研究角度审视强化学习，涉及经典/巴甫洛夫条件作用、操作性条件作用、Rescorla–Wagner 模型与 TD 模型等，为定义中列举的具体交叉主题提供出处。
直接说明心理学历史上依赖动物学习实验，以及后来转向研究思维、推理等认知过程，锚定定义中关于心理学作为研究行为与认知的学科及其历史演变的核心表述。

processed.definition: 神经科学是研究神经系统的多学科科学领域，探讨神经系统如何调节身体功能、控制行为、在发育、学习与衰老过程中如何变化，以及实现这些功能的细胞与分子机制。它与强化学习长期深度互动——许多RL核心算法最初受生物学习系统启发，而RL也为大脑奖赏系统（如多巴胺的奖励预测误差假说与TD误差的对应）提供了有影响力的计算模型。

supporting_observations.support: 直接提供神经科学的学科定义（多学科研究神经系统，涵盖身体功能调节、行为控制、随发育/学习/衰老的变化以及细胞与分子机制），锚定义第一句的核心内涵。
明确指出RL与神经科学（含心理学）'strongly interacted, with substantial benefits going both ways'，并提到RL为大脑奖赏系统贡献了有影响力的模型，支持定义第二句中双向互动的概括。
将奖励预测误差假说与多巴胺阵发活动相联系，并指出大脑可能实现类似actor–critic的算法，为定义第二句中'多巴胺的奖励预测误差机制与TD误差对应'这一具体比较提供原文事实。
说明第三部分对RL与神经科学关系的综述定位，支撑定义中将其与强化学习的互动作为该学科在此语境下显著识别特征的描述。

processed.definition: 统计学是研究数据的收集、分析、推断与解释的数学学科，在人工智能与机器学习的发展中，它是与这些领域长期交叉融合的核心数学基础之一（与优化等学科并列）。

supporting_observations.support: 原文将 statistics 与 optimization 并称为 'mathematical subjects'，明确其作为数学学科的上位类别，并指出 AI 与 ML 正在数十年时间尺度上与之融合，为定义中'数学学科'身份与'AI/ML 长期交叉融合'的表述提供直接文本依据。

processed.definition: 数学最优化（Optimization）是一个数学学科分支，其核心是建立用以寻找使目标函数（objective function）取得最优值之解的方法体系；它作为数学学科与统计学等并列存在，长期被工程、建筑等领域用于设计求解，并被强化学习等机器学习方法作为理论基础。

supporting_observations.support: 原文将 optimization 与 statistics 并列称为人工智能和机器学习数十年间不断融合的'mathematical subjects'，直接支持其作为数学学科的身份以及与统计学等并列的定位。
原文指出'reinforcement learning is based on optimization, it inherits the plusses and minuses of all optimization methods'以及'devising objective functions'问题，锚定最优化作为方法论体系及其与目标函数的核心关系。

原文将 optimization 描述为'class of mathematical methods that find solutions to satisfy an objective function'，并提到'optimization has been used for hundreds of years by engineers, architects, and others'，支撑其作为方法体系及其在工程建筑领域的长期应用。

processed.definition: 人工智能是一个致力于研究开发能执行类人智能任务（如学习、推理、搜索与决策）的计算系统与方法的学科领域，长期呈现出与统计学、优化等数学方法深度融合的趋势，并已回归对学习、搜索与决策等通用原理的系统性追求。

supporting_observations.support: 直接锚定人工智能作为一门学科（discipline），明确表述了'数十年来与统计学、优化等数学方法深度融合的趋势'以及'回归对学习、搜索与决策等通用原理追求'的两大趋势特征，是当前定义中趋势性描述的原文依据。
将人工智能表述为一个应用领域（field），提及'正在取得重大进展'且'应用正在改变数百万人的生活'，支撑定义中关于其作为学科领域并产出实际智能系统的含义。
将人工智能描述为一个广泛的技术领域（technology field），包含强化学习等多种方法路径，提及'取代就业岗位'等社会议题与'收益可超过破坏'的判断，支撑定义中对其学科广度的认定。

processed.definition: 机器学习是人工智能的一个重要子领域，研究使计算机系统能够从数据或经验中自动学习并改进性能的算法与方法。它包含监督学习、强化学习等多种学习形式，与人工神经网络、模式识别和统计曲线拟合等学科密切相关，现已成为推动人工智能应用落地的关键技术之一。

supporting_observations.support: 明确指出机器学习是一个包含强化学习在内的多种学习形式共存的学科领域，为定义中'包含监督学习、强化学习等多种学习形式'提供了直接依据。
将监督学习描述为机器学习的主要研究主题，并将机器学习与人工神经网络、模式识别、统计曲线拟合并列为相关领域，为定义中'与人工神经网络、模式识别和统计曲线拟合等学科密切相关'提供了原文支持。
将机器学习定位为人工智能领域的一部分，并指出它已成为一项关键关键技术，为定义中'人工智能的重要子领域'和'关键技术之一'提供了直接支持。

processed.definition: 在强化学习中，策略（policy）是智能体在给定环境状态下选择动作的行为规则，形式上是从感知到的状态到动作的映射，常以 π(a|s) 表示在状态 s 下选择动作 a 的概率；它可为确定性或随机性，并可通过查表或参数化函数（如神经网络）等方式实现。策略是强化学习系统的四大核心子要素之一（与奖励信号、价值函数和可选的环境模型并列），其本身即足以决定智能体的行为，也是各种强化学习算法（包括基于价值函数的方法和直接在策略空间搜索的进化方法）所共同学习与改进的对象。

supporting_observations.support: 提供了策略的核心定义：状态到动作的映射、对应心理学中的刺激—反应规则、可随机化、单独即足以决定行为；并明确它是强化学习系统四个主要子要素之一。
给出策略的正式数学定义：状态到动作概率的映射，以 π(a|s) 表示，对每个状态 s 给出 A(s) 上的概率分布，确认其作为价值函数定义所依赖的对象。
在第 3 章总结中将策略概括为'智能体根据状态选择动作的随机规则'，再次确认其作为 RL 系统中智能体行为决定者的核心地位。
说明策略的近似表示方式：在小规模有限状态集合下可用表（tabular case），大规模下需用更紧凑的参数化函数表示（神经网络、决策树等）。
明确策略是强化学习方法所搜索与评估的对象，无论进化方法还是基于价值函数的方法，都在'策略空间'中进行搜索并向最优策略收敛。

processed.definition: 价值函数是强化学习中用于估计从某状态（或状态—动作对）出发、在给定策略下所能获得的期望累积未来奖励（回报）的函数，刻画的是状态的长期好坏；它有别于即时奖励信号，是几乎所有强化学习算法中需要从交互经验中学习估计的最核心组成部分。

supporting_observations.support: 原文给出价值函数在RL中的标准定义——'specifies what is good in the long run'、'value of a state is the total amount of reward an agent can expect to accumulate over the future'、需要从观察序列中估计、'the most important component of almost all reinforcement learning algorithms'，是当前义项最权威的锚定。
给出状态价值函数 v_π(s) = E_π[G_t | S_t = s] 的形式化定义，锚定definition中'期望累积未来奖励'与'给定策略'两点。
明确'value and value function are key to most of the reinforcement learning methods'，并指出'使用价值函数是强化学习方法区别于进化方法的关键'，支持'几乎所有强化学习算法核心组成部分'这一表述。
给出策略价值函数对 v_π 与 q_π 的标准说明——'assign to each state, or state–action pair, the expected return'，锚定'状态或状态—动作对'和'期望回报'两要素。
指出价值函数是有限MDP框架的主要思想之一，贝尔曼方程与之配套，支撑该概念作为RL基础理论构件的身份。

processed.definition: Model of the environment is a component of a reinforcement learning system that mimics the environment's behavior so that, given a state and action, it can predict the resultant next state and next reward; it is used by model-based methods for planning, in contrast to model-free methods that learn purely by trial and error.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the foundational definition from §1.3: 'the fourth and final element of some reinforcement learning systems…mimics the behavior of the environment…given a state and action, the model might predict the resultant next state and next reward. Models are used for planning.'

Restates the definition in §8.1 in expanded form ('anything that an agent can use to predict how the environment will respond to its actions') and introduces the distinction between distribution models and sample models, both of which fall under the same concept.

Decomposes the environment model into a state-transition part and a reward-model part and reiterates its role in planning for model-based algorithms, anchoring the two-part structure used in the definition.

Notes that environment models can be acquired by supervised learning without reward signals and later used to plan behavior, supporting the claim that they are learned/predictive components rather than required parts of RL.
Reinforces the planning role of models and the sample-model vs. distribution-model split within Chapter 8, confirming that both forms are recognized variants of the same underlying concept.

processed.definition: Model-based methods are a class of reinforcement learning approaches that use an environment model—predicting next states and rewards given current states and actions—to decide on actions through planning, in contrast to model-free methods that learn purely from trial-and-error interaction. They are exemplified by dynamic programming, heuristic search, and integrated architectures such as Dyna; both families compute value functions, but model-based methods rely on planning as their primary computational component while model-free methods primarily rely on learning.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the canonical textbook statement equating model-based methods with the use of models and planning, and explicitly contrasts them with model-free trial-and-error learners.

Names dynamic programming and heuristic search as instances of model-based methods and states the key distinction that model-based methods rely on planning as their primary component while model-free methods rely on learning, with both sharing value-function computation.
Clarifies that the model need not be given a priori but can be learned, and that model-free methods serve as building blocks for model-based methods.
Cites the Dyna architecture as a concrete model-based approach and describes model-based methods as working together with model-free methods in the book's overall approach.

Reiterates the defining mechanism: model-based methods select actions as the result of planning ahead using a model of the agent's environment, and notes the correspondence to goal-directed behavior in psychology.

processed.definition: Model-free methods are a class of reinforcement learning methods that learn values or policies directly from real experience without constructing or using an explicit model of the environment's transitions and rewards. They are typically trial-and-error learners—exemplified by Monte Carlo and temporal-difference methods—and are contrasted with model-based methods, which instead rely on planning through an environment model.

supporting_observations.support: 提供最基础的对立定义：model-free methods 是 'simpler... explicitly trial-and-error learners—viewed as almost the opposite of planning'，与使用模型做 planning 的 model-based methods 对立。
明确 'do not need any kind of environment model at all'，并以井字棋选手为例说明 model-free 含义；同时指出当构建准确模型是瓶颈时 model-free 有优势，且可作为 model-based 的 building block。
指出 model-free 包含 Monte Carlo 和 temporal-difference 等方法，并强调 'model-free methods primarily rely on learning'（与 model-based 的 planning 形成对比），核心仍是 value function 的计算。
给出更具体的实现描述：'Model-free algorithms make decisions by accessing information that has been stored in a policy or an action-value function'，直接锚定 model-free 区别于 model-based 的行为方式。
全书总结段落中重申 model-free 与 model-based methods 并存于 Dyna 架构中，确认二者是同一 RL 框架下平行的方法类别，而非互斥或局部术语。

processed.definition: 随机策略是强化学习中一种策略，它在每个状态为各个动作指定选择概率 π(a|s)，而非确定性地选取单一动作；与确定性策略相对，随机策略不仅可作为探索手段，在不完全信息博弈或函数近似等场景下也可能本身就是最优策略的形式。

supporting_observations.support: 在第1章总览中首次给出随机策略的核心定义：'policies may be stochastic, specifying probabilities for each action'，确立了其与确定性策略的对立关系，并明确策略是强化学习智能体行为的核心要素。
在第4章策略改进中给出形式化记号 π(a|s)——在每个状态 s 下为每个动作 a 指定概率——并明确指出这是确定性策略情形的推广，策略改进定理在随机策略下同样成立，强化了'概率化选择'这一稳定特征。
在第5章蒙特卡洛方法中具体说明随机策略的一种典型用途：所有动作概率非零的随机策略可保证充分探索，是探索性应用场景的原文证据。
在第13章策略梯度方法中明确说明随机策略可以本身就是最优策略形式（如扑克中 bluffing），且函数近似下最优近似策略常为随机形式，soft-max 参数化可实现任意概率分布选择——这支持定义中'随机策略可能本身即为最优形式'的表述。

processed.definition: 价值估计是强化学习中由智能体依据其终身与环境交互所产生的观测序列，对各状态（或状态–动作对）的价值进行估计和反复更新（重估计）的过程；它通常被视为几乎所有强化学习算法中最核心的组成部分，其作用在于将基于即时奖励的原始信号转化为可指导长程决策的价值判断。

supporting_observations.support: 该观察直接给出价值估计的规范定义——'从智能体一生观测序列中估计和重估计价值的过程'，并明确其为'几乎所有强化学习算法中最重要的组成部分'以及过去六十年强化学习最重要的认识；原文还支撑了价值是奖励的预测、决策依据是价值判断而非即时奖励等关键事实，这些都已纳入解释。

processed.definition: 状态是强化学习中表征环境在某一时刻情形的信息，用作智能体决策的依据，也是策略和价值函数的输入以及模型的输入与输出。其形式化定义由马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）框架给出，通常要求该信号满足马尔可夫性。

supporting_observations.support: 直接提供核心定义：状态是向智能体传达'环境如何'的信号，是策略和价值函数的输入，也是模型的输入与输出；其正式定义由 MDP 框架给出。该观察锚定了定义中关于'信号/输入/输出'以及'MDP 形式化'的核心要点。
明确状态是智能体在每个时间步接收到的环境表征，并提出马尔可夫性要求（状态须包含对未来有影响的所有过去交互信息），支持定义中关于'MDP 形式化'与'通常要求满足马尔可夫性'的表述。
将状态与动作、奖励并列为 MDP 框架的三个定义性要素，支持定义中状态作为 MDP 框架基本构件的定位。
说明智能体动作会影响环境的未来状态，进而影响后续可用的行动和机会，支持定义中状态作为'决策依据'以及智能体与环境交互语境的角色。
在第 3 章总结中将状态明确定义为'选择动作所依据的基础'（the basis for making the choices），直接支持定义首句中'用作智能体决策的依据'的表述。

processed.definition: Evolutionary methods are a class of optimization solution methods, exemplified by genetic algorithms, genetic programming, and simulated annealing, that search directly in the space of policies by holding policies fixed, evaluating each over many episodes in separate instances of the environment, and carrying the highest-reward policies (with random variations) into the next generation. Unlike value-function-based reinforcement learning methods, they do not learn during individual policy lifetimes and do not exploit the state-to-action structure of the problem.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the core definition: names the method class (genetic algorithms, genetic programming, simulated annealing), the mechanism of applying multiple static policies over extended periods, retaining highest-reward variants across generations, and the biological-evolution analogy with no learning during individual lifetimes.

Illustrates the typical implementation pattern—direct search in policy space via hill-climbing or maintaining and evaluating a population of policies—which is the canonical operational form of evolutionary methods in RL.

Specifies the evaluation convention (hold policy fixed, use whole-episode outcomes like win frequency) and the key distinction from value-function methods: only final outcomes are used and within-episode structure is ignored.

Provides the textbook's summary characterization—searching directly in policy space guided by evaluations of entire policies—offering the cleanest single-sentence contrast with value-function-based RL methods.

processed.definition: 遗传算法是一类受生物进化过程启发的优化/搜索方法，属于进化方法的范畴，通过在候选解（如策略、表示或参数）的种群上进行选择、变异与逐代演化来寻找较优解；在强化学习语境中，它常被用作不估计值函数而直接在策略空间或表示空间进行搜索的替代方法。

supporting_observations.support: 明确将遗传算法归入进化方法类，描述其不估计值函数、通过对多组静态策略按奖励筛选并以随机变异传递到下一代来求解强化学习问题，为定义中'进化方法'类属、不依赖值函数、代际演化策略等关键特征提供原文锚定。
在 Holland 分类器系统语境中直接称遗传算法为'一个进化方法'，其作用是'演化有用的表示'，支持定义中将'表示空间'与'策略空间'并列为典型搜索目标。
描述遗传风格算法维护并评估一个策略种群，而不是对单一策略进行逐步精炼，锚定定义中'候选解种群'这一稳定特征。
将遗传算法定位为'进化方法'，并与梯度下降和人工神经网络方法进行对比，指出进化方法在学习过程中可利用的细节信息较少，支持定义中'优化/搜索方法'的定性以及与梯度类方法相对的方法学位置。
记载 Mukundan 和 Martínez (2012) 用遗传算法推导更复杂的奖励函数，表明遗传算法在强化学习教材中也作为通用的优化工具使用，支持定义中'优化方法'这一上位类属，而非仅限于策略/表示演化。

processed.definition: Genetic programming is an evolutionary computation method that evolves candidate solutions—typically represented as program-like structures—through selection, crossover, and mutation operations inspired by natural selection. In reinforcement learning, it is grouped among the evolutionary methods that solve problems without estimating value functions, instead carrying the highest-reward policies and random variations of them forward across successive generations.

supporting_observations.support: Directly anchors the RL-context characterization: genetic programming is listed alongside genetic algorithms, simulated annealing, and other optimization methods as a solution method that never estimates value functions; it applies multiple static policies, keeps the highest-reward ones and their random variations, and repeats over generations—an operation the source explicitly compares to biological evolution.

Provides the canonical formulation and origin: Koza (1992), 'Genetic Programming: On the Programming of Computers by Means of Natural Selection,' which grounds the 'programming of computers by means of natural selection' framing and the natural-selection mechanism underlying the method.

processed.definition: 模拟退火是一类受物理退火过程启发的概率优化（元启发式）方法，通过以随温度下降而递减的概率接受较差解来搜索全局近似最优解。在强化学习语境下，它与遗传算法、遗传编程一同被归入广义的"进化方法"，不通过估计价值函数，而是通过对多组静态策略的评估、保留与变异迭代来求解强化学习问题。

supporting_observations.support: 原文将模拟退火与遗传算法、遗传编程并列为'solution methods … that never estimate value functions'，并由上下文说明这些方法通过对多组静态策略的评估、保留与变异迭代来获得高回报策略，被合称为'evolutionary methods'，支撑了定义中其作为'不估计价值函数的优化方法'以及在 RL 语境下属于'进化方法'的描述。

processed.definition: In reinforcement learning, a preprocessing system is the (hypothetical) component, nominally part of the agent's environment, that transforms raw environment information into the state signal available to the agent's policy and value function. The book treats it as a fixed abstraction and does not address how to construct, change, or learn it, in order to concentrate on decision-making rather than state-representation design.

supporting_observations.support: Source passage directly states that the state signal is 'produced by some preprocessing system that is nominally part of the agent's environment' and that the book deliberately does not address constructing, changing, or learning it (except briefly in Section 17.3), supporting both the identity of the system as the environment-to-state-signal mapping and the scope limitation of the definition.

processed.definition: Tic-tac-toe is a two-player paper-and-pencil game played on a three-by-three grid in which opponents alternate marking Xs and Os, with the goal of placing three of one's own marks in a row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally before the other; a board that fills up with no such row is a draw, and the game is widely used as a pedagogical example in fields such as reinforcement learning because of its small, finite state space and naturally episodic play.

supporting_observations.support: Directly anchors the core definition: two players, three-by-three board, alternating Xs and Os, win by three in a row (horizontal, vertical, diagonal), and a filled board with no three-in-a-row is a draw.

Supports the claim that tic-tac-toe has a 'relatively small, finite state set' and that play decomposes into discrete episodes (individual games with reward only at the end), which explains its frequent use as a pedagogical example.

Confirms tic-tac-toe is a general game (with 'basic moves of the game' and positions related by 'symmetries') rather than an artifact of any particular algorithm, and provides the Chinese alias '井字棋' for cross-lingual identification.

processed.definition: Minimax is a classical game-theoretic solution for sequential decision problems, typically applied to two-player zero-sum games, in which a player chooses moves to minimize its maximum possible loss (or maximize its minimum gain) under the assumption that the opponent plays optimally. A notable consequence is that a minimax player will avoid any state from which it could lose against an optimal opponent, even if in practice the opponent's sub-optimal play would always lead to a win from that state.

supporting_observations.support: The passage explicitly identifies the entity as 'the classical minimax solution from game theory' for 'sequential decision problems' and provides the defining property that it 'assumes a particular way of playing by the opponent' and that 'a minimax player would never reach a game state from which it could lose, even if in fact it always won from that state because of incorrect play by the opponent.'

processed.definition: Game theory is the classical discipline that studies strategic interactions between players or agents, covering both cooperative (team) and competitive settings. It provides principled solution concepts—such as the minimax solution—for games by typically assuming particular models or styles of opponent play.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the definition's characterization of game theory as a classical discipline and its association with the minimax solution that assumes a particular way of playing by the opponent.
Anchors the definition's scope of game theory as encompassing both cooperative (team) and competitive games, and the non-trivial aspect of determining the best collective action.

processed.definition: Dynamic programming is a classical optimization framework, introduced by Richard Bellman in the 1950s, for solving sequential decision problems by recursively decomposing them into overlapping subproblems and applying the associated Bellman (or Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman) equation. In reinforcement learning it denotes a well-developed class of model-based methods for finite Markov decision processes that require a complete and accurate distribution model of the environment, compute optimal policies by performing bootstrapping expected updates on state values (as in policy evaluation, policy iteration, and value iteration), and constitute the theoretical foundation from which model-free methods such as Monte Carlo and temporal-difference learning are derived.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the general identity of the concept: a class of methods for solving optimal control problems by solving the Bellman equation, developed by Bellman in the mid-1950s, and extends the Hamilton–Jacobi theory.

Provides the canonical RL-context definition: a collection of algorithms that compute optimal policies given a perfect model of the environment as an MDP, and supplies the term 'DP' as the standard abbreviation.

Enumerates the core identifying algorithms (policy evaluation, policy improvement, policy iteration, value iteration) and the characteristic mechanism: classical DP operates via sweeps through the state set performing expected updates based on successor-state probabilities.

Places DP in the RL taxonomy as one of the three fundamental classes of methods (with Monte Carlo and temporal-difference learning) and reiterates the cross-cutting property of requiring a complete and accurate model of the environment.

Supports the contrastive identifying feature that DP is the prototypical bootstrapping method (updating estimates from other learned estimates without waiting for a final outcome), explicitly positioning it as one of the two pillars that TD learning combines.

processed.definition: Exploratory move is an action type in reinforcement learning in which the agent selects at random from among the non-greedy (non-exploiting) actions, in order to experience states that would otherwise never be visited. Unlike greedy moves, exploratory moves do not themselves trigger value updates or learning, but they expose the agent to new states that inform future estimation.

supporting_observations.support: The source text defines exploratory moves as actions selected randomly from among the non-greedy moves in order to 'experience states that we might otherwise never see' (P000044), and states explicitly that 'Exploratory moves do not result in any learning' while the other (greedy) moves cause value updates (P000048). Together these passages anchor both the selection rule and the non-learning/contrast-with-greedy aspects of the definition.

processed.definition: In reinforcement learning, a greedy move (or greedy action) is the action that, at a given decision point, is chosen by selecting from the available alternatives the one with the highest estimated value under the agent's current value estimates, thereby exploiting rather than exploring. It is the standard exploitation component in policies such as ε-greedy action selection and is defined uniformly whether the values are stored on successor states (as in the tic-tac-toe example) or on state–action pairs as action values Q_t(a) or approximate action values q̂(s, a, w).

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the original formulation of greedy move in the tic-tac-toe example: selecting the move leading to the state with the greatest value (highest estimated probability of winning) and triggering value backups of the earlier state toward the later state's value.

Provides the standard action-value formulation: at any time step, a greedy action is one whose estimated value Q_t(a) is greatest, and choosing it is called exploiting current knowledge—directly paralleling the tic-tac-toe definition and introducing the exploitation/exploration contrast.

Reinforces that greedy actions 'look best at present' under current estimates and links the concept to ε-greedy action selection, supporting the use of greedy moves as the exploitation half of exploration–exploitation strategies.

Gives the formal argmax definition in the function-approximation setting, A*_{t+1} = argmax_a q̂(S_{t+1}, a, w_t), showing the concept generalizes to approximate action values and confirming identity with the bandit greedy action.

Shows the term used as the action selected under a greedy policy in the eligibility-trace setting (Watkins's Q(λ)), confirming that greedy action/move is a stable cross-chapter RL concept and not tied to a single chapter's example.

processed.definition: An opponent model is a representation of another agent's (opponent's) behavior used in game-theoretic and multi-agent decision-making, which can be combined with planning methods such as dynamic programming to compute an optimal solution. Because a complete specification of the opponent is typically not available a priori, the model is usually an approximation, obtained either by learning from experience (e.g., by playing many games) or by careful hand-construction.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the general meaning: the text explicitly defines learning 'a model of the opponent's behavior, up to some level of confidence' and then 'apply[ing] dynamic programming to compute an optimal solution given the approximate opponent model,' while noting that a full opponent specification is 'not available a priori' but 'can be estimated from experience.'

Demonstrates that an opponent model need not be learned from self-play; the passage describes 'carefully-crafted models of human players' used in Watson's Jeopardy! system, confirming that the concept extends to hand-constructed stochastic process models of the opponent.

processed.definition: Hill climbing is a local search optimization procedure that iteratively generates and evaluates candidate solutions, moving to neighboring solutions that yield incremental improvements in an objective function. In reinforcement learning it is commonly applied in policy space to successively improve policies and is often used as a mechanism within evolutionary methods.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the core mechanism of hill climbing (successively generating and evaluating solutions for incremental improvements) and its role as a typical way to implement an evolutionary method, here illustrated with tic-tac-toe policy search.

processed.definition: A one-step temporal-difference (TD) value update rule in reinforcement learning, written as V(St) ← V(St) + α[Rt+1 + γV(St+1) − V(St)], which shifts the estimated value of a state a fraction α toward the TD target composed of the immediate reward and the discounted estimated value of the next state. It is the simplest TD method (also known as TD(0) or one-step TD) and appears in its reward-free, undiscounted form V(St) ← V(St) + α[V(St+1) − V(St)] in the textbook's tic-tac-toe example, where intermediate rewards are zero and γ = 1.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the original tic-tac-toe backup rule V(St) ← V(St) + α[V(St+1) − V(St)], explaining the role of α and the notation St, St+1; this is the local instance that the broader TD(0) update reduces to when intermediate rewards are zero.

States the general one-step TD update V(St) ← V(St) + α[Rt+1 + V(St+1) − V(St)] and explicitly names it TD(0) / one-step TD, anchoring the general form (with reward Rt+1) that the tic-tac-toe formula specializes.
Defines the TD(0) update as St ↦ Rt+1 + v̂(St+1, wt), independently confirming the TD target structure (immediate reward + estimated value of next state) used in the general update formula.
Identifies TD(0) as the one-step sample-update counterpart of dynamic programming for policy evaluation, reinforcing its identity as the simplest one-step TD rule.

processed.definition: In reinforcement learning, the step-size parameter (commonly denoted α) is a positive scalar that weights the error term in incremental update rules, controlling how much an estimate moves toward its target on each update; it appears in the general form NewEstimate ← OldEstimate + α[Target − OldEstimate] used across temporal-difference learning, bandit methods, Q-learning/Sarsa, and stochastic gradient methods, and may be held constant, decayed over time, or made state- or action-dependent (α_t(a)), with its scheduling governing convergence.

supporting_observations.support: Establishes the general incremental update form NewEstimate ← OldEstimate + StepSize[Target − OldEstimate], states the notation α (and more generally α_t(a)), and notes that in the incremental sample-average method the step size changes from time step to time step.

Source of the original definition: explicitly defines α as a 'small positive fraction called the step-size parameter' that 'influences the rate of learning' in the temporal-difference update rule, and links proper decay to convergence.
Introduces the constant step-size parameter α ∈ (0, 1] as the typical choice for nonstationary problems, showing the parameter can be held fixed across updates.

States the convergence behavior tied to the parameter: TD(0) converges in the mean for a sufficiently small constant α, and with probability 1 if α decreases according to the stochastic approximation conditions (2.7).
Shows the parameter is referred to as the 'usual positive step-size parameter' in Q-learning-like sample updates, confirming cross-algorithm reuse beyond TD prediction.

processed.definition: 它是强化学习中通过自举（bootstrapping）更新价值估计的一类学习方法，其核心机制是利用同一量在两个连续时刻的估计之差（即时序差分 V(St+1)−V(St)）来即时调整较早时刻的估计，而不需等到回合结束，也不依赖环境模型。

supporting_observations.support: 直接给出定义性表述——更新基于'两个连续时刻估计之差 V(St+1)−V(St)'，并以 V(St)←V(St)+α[V(St+1)−V(St)] 为具体示例，锚定本概念的核心更新机制。
明确将 TD learning 描述为'蒙特卡洛思想与动态规划（DP）思想的结合'，能'直接从原始经验中学习而无需环境模型'，并通过'基于其他学到的估计进行更新（自举）'来锚定 bootstrapping 与 model-free 两大识别特征。
将 TD learning 列为'求解有限马尔可夫决策过程三大基础方法类之一'，并指出其'不需要模型、完全可增量计算'，确立其在强化学习方法谱系中的位置与两项关键性质。
给出简洁的一步更新机制：'TD 方法只需等到下一时间步，在 t+1 即可利用观测到的奖励 Rt+1 和下一状态的估计 V(St+1) 构成目标并立即做有用更新'，直接支撑'不需等到回合结束'这一识别特征。
强调 TD 方法'独特之处在于由同一量在时间上相邻的估计之差驱动'，例如井字棋中对获胜概率的相邻估计之差，锚定'时序差分'作为概念名称的字面来源。

processed.definition: A class of reinforcement learning methods that learn a value function to evaluate individual states during the course of play, in contrast to evolutionary methods that rely only on final outcomes; both ultimately search the space of policies, but value function methods additionally exploit information available during play.

supporting_observations.support: The passage directly contrasts evolutionary methods (which only use final game outcomes) with value function methods (which allow individual states to be evaluated), and states that both search the space of policies while value function methods exploit information available during play—exactly the three claims carried in the definition.

processed.definition: An artificial neural network (ANN) is a computational model composed of interconnected units that loosely mimic the properties of biological neurons, widely used as a nonlinear function approximator in supervised learning, pattern recognition, and reinforcement learning. It generalizes from training examples to produce outputs for previously unseen inputs, which makes it suitable for problems with very large or high-dimensional state or input spaces, and modern multi-layer variants trained by backpropagation and stochastic gradient methods underpin deep learning and deep reinforcement learning.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the original use case (Tesauro combining an ANN with TD learning for backgammon with ~10^20 states) and the key functional property of generalizing from experience to unseen states, which is central to why ANNs are used in large-space problems.

Provides the clearest structural definition directly from the source: 'a network of interconnected units that have some of the properties of neurons,' and identifies ANN as a standard method for nonlinear function approximation, anchoring the first sentence of the definition.

Identifies ANNs as nonlinear function approximation methods trained by backpropagation and variants of SGD, and links them to deep reinforcement learning, supporting the second sentence's mention of multi-layer variants and modern training methods.

Classifies ANNs as a popular function approximation method whose outputs extrapolate from observed targets (i.e., it is not an averager), reinforcing the description of ANNs as a general nonlinear function-approximation method beyond any single application.

Index entry showing 'ANN, see artificial neural networks' cross-references to many sections (223–228, 436–450, 472), confirming ANN is treated as a single general-purpose model class used across supervised learning, function approximation, and deep RL in this book.

processed.definition: A single-agent problem setting in which the environment behaves stochastically—like 'nature'—rather than as a strategic adversary, so there is no external opponent to model. In the reinforcement learning literature it is contrasted with two-person games such as tic-tac-toe to show that RL is not restricted to adversarial, multi-agent settings.

supporting_observations.support: The passage directly defines a 'game against nature' as the case 'in which there is no external adversary,' explicitly contrasting it with the two-person game tic-tac-toe, which anchors both the single-agent/non-adversarial nature and the RL contrastive purpose used in the definition.

processed.definition: Backgammon is a two-player stochastic board game played worldwide with 15 white and 15 black pieces on a board of 24 points, in which players move pieces according to dice rolls and bear them off the board; it has approximately 10^20 possible states and an effective branching factor of about 400, making it a canonical large-scale benchmark in reinforcement learning research (e.g., Tesauro's TD-Gammon and rollout algorithms).

supporting_observations.support: Provides the core game description: 15 white and 15 black pieces on 24 points, stochastic, played worldwide with world championships; also notes the enormous state space that precludes conventional heuristic search.

Anchors the ~10^20 state count and the canonical RL milestone (Tesauro's program surpassing previous programs and the world's best human players), establishing backgammon's status as a flagship RL benchmark.
Confirms the ~10^20 states figure and that the game's dynamics are accurately known and satisfy the Markov property, reinforcing its identity as the same board game discussed elsewhere.
Documents backgammon's large branching factor and the seconds-scale move time constraint, together with the TD-Gammon system, further identifying the same game.
Specifies the game's win conditions: reward is zero except upon winning, with special 'gammon' and 'backgammon' scoring outcomes, supplying concrete gameplay detail.

processed.definition: The tabula rasa view is the perspective, drawn from the 'blank slate' tradition, that learning and intelligence must be built entirely from experience, starting with no prior knowledge about the task. Within reinforcement learning this view is explicitly not entailed: prior information can instead be incorporated in a variety of ways that can be critical for efficient learning.

supporting_observations.support: The passage states that the tic-tac-toe learner 'started with no prior knowledge beyond the rules of the game, but reinforcement learning by no means entails a tabula rasa view of learning and intelligence,' and that 'prior information can be incorporated into reinforcement learning in a variety of ways that can be critical for efficient learning,' directly anchoring both the meaning of the tabula rasa view and its non-necessity in RL.

processed.definition: Deep learning is a machine learning paradigm and research subfield built on artificial neural networks with multiple layers, characterized by an emphasis on representation learning. In the context of reinforcement learning it is cited as one approach—alongside ANNs generally—for providing generalization and parametric function approximation, but the source notes it is not the only or necessarily best way and that current methods still struggle to learn rapidly in fully incremental, online settings.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the general characterization of deep learning as the current stage in the history of ANNs with emphasis on representation learning, and distinguishes it from earlier error-backpropagation stages.
Cites Schmidhuber's 'Deep learning in neural networks: An overview', anchoring deep learning as an established research subfield within neural network research.
Supports the claim that, within reinforcement learning, deep learning is one way to provide generalization alongside ANNs and is not the only or necessarily best way.
Supports the link between deep learning and function approximation extensions of tabular RL methods (e.g., TD methods), confirming its role in approximating value functions.
Directly supports the claim that current deep learning methods are a major step in parametric function approximation but struggle to learn rapidly in fully incremental, online RL settings.

processed.definition: In reinforcement learning, generalization is the ability of an agent to transfer knowledge from previously encountered states to new but similar states, so as to act sensibly in states it has never seen before. It is the central issue in problems with very large or combinatorial state spaces and is typically realized through function approximation borrowed from supervised learning, in which updating the value estimate at one state propagates to affect the estimates of many other states.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the most comprehensive statement in the Part II introduction: generalization is the key issue for large state spaces, requires generalizing from similar states to make sensible decisions in unseen ones, and is linked to function approximation as its standard realization mechanism.

Anchors the core meaning at first introduction (Tic-Tac-Toe example): generalization as selecting appropriate actions in new states from information saved at similar past states, and ties it to the difficulty of very large state sets.

Specifies the mechanism by which generalization is achieved through function approximation: a single-state update propagates to change the estimated values of many other states, making learning more powerful but also harder to manage.

Formalizes the strength of generalization between any two states via the kernel function k(s, s'), showing that the concept is quantitative and can be expressed independently of any particular approximator.

Confirms the framing of generalization as a capability RL systems must possess to be applicable to large-scale AI or engineering problems, explicitly enabled by supervised-learning function approximation.

processed.definition: In reinforcement learning, a hidden state is a component of the environment's underlying state that is not directly observable by the agent, so that reinforcement learning methods must still operate when only partial information is available or when distinct true states appear indistinguishable to the learner.

supporting_observations.support: The passage directly defines hidden state by contrasting the tic-tac-toe setting, where 'we have access to the true state,' with cases where 'part of the state is hidden' or 'different states appear to the learner to be the same,' anchoring the concept to unobservable state components in RL.

processed.definition: In reinforcement learning, an episodic task is a problem setting in which the agent–environment interaction naturally breaks into a series of separate episodes, each ending in a terminal state and followed by a reset to a standard starting state or distribution, with a finite (but possibly episode-dependent) number of time steps per episode. It is typically contrasted with a continuing task, in which interaction proceeds indefinitely without termination, and is the natural setting for the undiscounted (γ = 1) return formulation.

supporting_observations.support: Provides the canonical definition: agent–environment interaction breaks naturally into episodes, each ending in a terminal state, followed by reset to a standard start state or distribution, with termination time T a random variable varying across episodes.

Adds the formal structure: each episode is a finite sequence of time steps, and the key mathematical property that each action affects only a finite number of subsequent rewards — the property that makes episodic tasks mathematically easier than continuing ones.
Reinforces the 'all episodes eventually terminate no matter what actions are selected' requirement, which is what guarantees well-defined returns and makes methods such as Monte Carlo applicable.
Anchors the identity of episodic tasks by tying them to the undiscounted return formulation and explicitly contrasting them with continuing tasks in which interaction continues without limit.

Provides the canonical illustrative example (separate games of tic-tac-toe with reward only at the end) and the explicit contrast that RL is not restricted to such episodes but also applies when behavior continues indefinitely with rewards of any magnitude at any time.

processed.definition: 分层学习系统是按层次结构组织学习过程的系统架构，将学习任务分解到不同层级，使得学习可以同时在多个层次上进行；其中较高层级的"动作"本身可以由低层级的策略或问题求解方法组成，常用于强化学习等需要多时间尺度决策的场景。

supporting_observations.support: 该 Observation 提供了核心原文支撑：'In hierarchical learning systems, reinforcement learning can work simultaneously on several levels' 直接锚定了'多层次同时学习'这一关键特征；其上下文关于高层级 action 本身可由 problem-solving method 构成的说法，支持了定义中关于高层动作由低层策略组合的描述。

processed.definition: 在强化学习中，动作（action）是指智能体（agent）在每个时间步基于当前状态从可用选项中所做出的选择，它与状态、奖励共同构成马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）框架的三大基本要素，用于刻画智能体与环境之间的交互接口；该选择会通过状态转移影响未来可用的行动与回报，其延迟且不确定的后果通常需要借助价值函数或策略进行规划。

supporting_observations.support: 直接说明动作与状态、奖励是 MDP 框架定义智能体与环境交互的三个基本术语，锚定'三大基本要素'和'刻画交互'的核心身份。
明确'智能体在时间步 t 基于状态 St 选取动作 At ∈ A(s)'，并指出动作会影响下一状态与奖励，支撑定义中'基于当前状态从可用选项中做出选择'及'影响未来状态与回报'的描述。
指出'动作是智能体做出的选择'，并与状态、奖励一起定义具体的智能体–环境接口任务，支撑定义中'选择'语义和'交互接口'定位。
将动作描述为 MDP 框架中在智能体与环境之间来回传递的信号之一（代表智能体的选择），与状态、奖励并列，进一步强化其作为框架基本信号的角色。
强调动作会影响环境的未来状态，从而影响后续可用的行动与机会，并需要考虑间接、延迟后果，支撑定义中关于'延迟且不确定后果需要规划'的说明。

processed.definition: The Bellman equation is a recursive functional equation that expresses a value function over a dynamical system's states in terms of itself, forming the mathematical core of dynamic programming and reinforcement learning. It appears in multiple forms—corresponding to state-value, action-value, optimal, differential, and options-based settings—and is typically operationalized by converting it into iterative update rules whose fixed point yields the desired value function.

supporting_observations.support: Anchors the core identity: a functional equation built from a dynamical system's state and a value function ('optimal return function'), introduced by Richard Bellman and central to dynamic programming.

Supports the claim that Bellman equations (including the Bellman optimality equations) are turned by DP algorithms into assignment-style update rules for iteratively improving value-function approximations.

Supports the 'multiple forms' aspect: there are four primary Bellman equations, one for each of the four primary value functions (v_π, v*, q_π, q*), with convergence of expected updates signaling that the corresponding Bellman equation is satisfied.
Supports the fixed-point characterization: the Bellman equation can be written as v = B_π v, identifying the value function as a fixed point of the Bellman operator B_π.
Index evidence that the Bellman equation family spans distinct concrete forms: for v_π, for q_π, for optimal value functions v* and q*, a differential form, and a form for options.

processed.definition: 策略迭代（Policy Iteration）是一种用于求解马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）的经典动态规划算法，由 Ronald Howard 于 1960 年提出，通过交替执行策略评估（policy evaluation）与策略改进（policy improvement）生成单调改进的策略与价值函数序列，在有限 MDP 上可在有限步迭代内收敛到最优策略与最优价值函数。

supporting_observations.support: 锚定概念起源：明确指出 Ronald Howard（1960）提出了用于 MDP 的 policy iteration method，是该算法的最初出处与历史定位。
给出算法的核心机制：交替执行 policy evaluation（E）与 policy improvement（I）形成 π₀ → v^{π₀} → π₁ → … → π* → v* 的单调改进序列，并证明有限 MDP 上经有限步迭代即可收敛到最优策略与最优价值函数。
确认其作为动态规划方法的上位类别定位：与 value iteration 并列被称为最常用的两种 DP 方法，并指出 policy improvement theorem 与 policy iteration algorithm 来源于 Bellman (1957a) 与 Howard (1960)，可用于在已知 MDP 完整知识下可靠地计算最优策略。
明确刻画两个子过程——使价值函数与当前策略一致的策略评估，以及使策略对当前价值函数贪心的策略改进——在策略迭代中严格交替、各自完整执行，并由此引出广义策略迭代（GPI）概念，体现其在 RL 理论体系中的核心地位。
补充其在实践中的地位：与 value iteration 并列为广泛使用的 DP 方法，实践收敛速度通常远快于理论最坏情形，且无明确证据表明在一般情况下何者更优，反映其作为基础 DP 算法的稳定特征。

processed.definition: The Law of Effect is a principle of learning formulated by Edward Thorndike (1911) stating that, in a given situation, responses followed by satisfying consequences become more firmly connected to that situation and are therefore more likely to recur, whereas responses followed by discomfort have their connections weakened. It is widely regarded as a foundational statement of trial-and-error learning through selectional and associative processes, and it has served as a key conceptual antecedent of reinforcement learning, influencing the learning theories of Clark Hull and the experimental methods of B. F. Skinner.

supporting_observations.support: Provides Thorndike's 1911 original statement (p. 244) — satisfaction strengthens the situation–response bond, discomfort weakens it — and the explicit reason Thorndike named it the Law of Effect: it describes the effect of reinforcing events on the tendency to select actions.

Establishes the Law of Effect's broader status as a basic principle underlying much behavior and its role as the basis of Hull's learning theories and Skinner's experimental methods of instrumental conditioning.

Identifies the Law of Effect as Thorndike's most influential law of learning, characterizing it as trial-and-error learning that is simultaneously selectional (trying and selecting among alternatives by their consequences) and associative (linking selected actions to situations/states).

Describes the Law of Effect in reinforcement-learning terms as describing associative search through the formation of associative links between situations (states) and actions, anchoring its identity as a situation–action selection principle.
Attributes the law to Thorndike's experiments with cats and other animals and situates it as the basis of trial-and-error learning in the control aspect of reinforcement learning.

processed.definition: Neurodynamic programming is a research area that combines dynamic programming with artificial neural networks and other function-approximation methods to address large-scale sequential decision and optimization problems. The term was coined by Dimitri Bertsekas and John Tsitsiklis in their 1996 monograph of the same name, and it is widely regarded as equivalent to what Bertsekas and others also call "approximate dynamic programming," sharing with reinforcement learning the goal of overcoming the classical shortcomings of exact dynamic programming.

supporting_observations.support: Directly anchors the core identity: the term 'neurodynamic programming' was coined by Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis in 1996 to denote the combination of dynamic programming and artificial neural networks, identifies it as a research area, and notes its equivalence with 'approximate dynamic programming' and its close relationship to reinforcement learning.

Confirms the 1996 Bertsekas & Tsitsiklis monograph 'Neuro-Dynamic Programming' (Athena Scientific) and broadens the combination to include 'other function-approximation methods' for handling large-scale problems, supporting the function-approximation aspect of the definition.

Anchors the equivalence between 'neurodynamic programming' and 'approximate dynamic programming' by showing that Bertsekas's later volumes (notably the 2012 Vol. 2 subtitled 'Approximate Dynamic Programming') are continuations of the same research program, justifying treating them as interchangeable names for the field.

Further supports treating 'approximate dynamic programming' as a co-referential term for the same entity, as the 'linear programming approach to approximate dynamic programming' (de Farias, Van Roy) is situated within this same research lineage.

processed.definition: 在动物学习心理学中，强化指由于动物在适当的时间关系上接收到某种刺激或经历刺激的省略（强化物），而使行为模式（通过增加其强度或频次）被加强并产生持久改变的现象；该概念后被部分心理学家扩展为也可涵盖使行为模式产生持久削弱的过程，并同时适用于经典条件反射与操作条件反射两类学习情境。

supporting_observations.support: Pavlov 1927 对强化的原始定义——在适当时间关系上接收刺激（强化物）导致行为模式加强——以及后来被部分心理学家扩展为也包括削弱，为本定义的核心义项提供直接原文依据。
明确指出强化用于描述经典条件反射和操作条件反射中的学习，并再次说明原本仅指加强、后来也用于削弱，支持定义中关于扩展含义与适用情境的说明。
给出传统定义的精确表述：行为模式通过强度或频次增加而被加强，源于动物在适当时间关系上接受刺激或经历刺激省略；并指出强化在移除后仍须留下持久改变，以及扩展到削弱含义的来源（Mackintosh, 1983），锚定定义中"持久改变"与"扩展到削弱"两处细节。

processed.entity: 强化物（动物学习心理学）
processed.definition: 在动物学习心理学中，强化物（reinforcer）是指在适当的时间关系下与另一刺激或反应相联系、能使动物行为产生持久加强或削弱作用的刺激，它既可以是在工具性条件作用中因动物行为而呈现的奖赏或惩罚，也可以是在经典条件作用中作为非条件刺激引发条件反应；仅吸引注意或暂时激活行为、但在撤除后不留下持久变化的刺激不构成强化物。

supporting_observations.support: 直接锚定核心定义：强化物是动物在适当时间关系下与另一刺激或反应相联系而接收到的刺激；强化/弱化效果必须在强化物撤除后仍持续，仅吸引注意或激活行为而无法产生持久变化的刺激不视为强化物。
补充"无论是否与动物先前行为相依"这一广义视角，说明强化物的判定标准是是否构成行为变化的原因，而非仅限行为相依情境，扩展了概念的应用边界。
说明强化物在工具性条件作用中的典型形态——其呈现与动物行为相依（奖赏或惩罚），与经典条件作用中刺激的非行为相依形成对比，支持解释中工具性条件作用的用途描述。
说明强化物在经典条件作用中的典型形态——非条件刺激（US）被称为强化物，因为它强化了动物对条件刺激产生条件反应的行为，支持解释中经典条件作用的用途描述。
术语总结视角再次确认强化物为"行为变化的原因性刺激"，并明确强化可同时涵盖加强与削弱两种方向，与本义项的"持久加强或削弱"表述一致。

processed.definition: 信用分配问题是强化学习中由 Minsky 于 1961 年提出的核心问题：在试错学习过程中，当最终的成功或奖励由一连串先后发生的决策（动作）共同产生时，如何将功劳（或责任）合理地回溯分配给各个中间决策。它主要因奖励信号与引发它的动作之间存在延迟而变得困难，书中讨论的资格迹、TD 方法以及 actor–critic 等机制都在不同程度上旨在解决该问题。

supporting_observations.support: 给出 Minsky (1961) "Steps Toward Artificial Intelligence" 中对 credit-assignment problem 的原始定义，并明确该问题面向复杂强化学习系统，是全书方法试图解决的核心问题。
在 Chapter 14.4 再次引用 Minsky (1961) 的原话作为问题定义，并补充指明该书用两类基本机制应对该问题：资格迹和用于学习价值函数的 TD 方法。
说明 actor–critic 方法中的 critic 通过提供逐时刻的条件性强化来缓解主奖励信号延迟，从而部分解决该问题，支撑定义中关于 actor–critic 是解决方案之一的表述。
说明 Holland 的 classifier systems 通过 bucket-brigade 算法来应对信用分配问题，并指出其与 TD 算法的关联，体现了该问题在 RL 早期多种方法中的核心地位。
